best_echo_sets.commentary: Best set for Aero Main DPS characters who can apply Aero Erosion or have an Aero Erosion applier on the team. Grants 10% Aero DMG Bonus and an extra 30% Aero DMG Bonus as well as 10% CRIT Rate for 10s when attacking targets inflicted with Aero Erosion. Offers an extra 10% CRIT Rate over the other Aero sets such as Gusts of Welkin or Sierra Gale, providing extra overall damage so long as Aero Erosion is present on the enemy. In teams without Aero Erosion appliers however, this set is useless comparatively to Sierra Gale.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: This Echo provides a free decent amount of Aero DMG when casting Outro Skill in all situations, provides 12% Aero DMG Bonus to Jiyan and while its Transform Active Skill is not used in Jiyan's rotations, it is the best Main Echo he has, albeit by a very small difference when compared to Reminiscence: Fleurdelys (pick what has the best substats overall!)

best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Aero DMG% boost and an additional 30% Aero DMG% after using the intro lasting 15 seconds for a grand total of 40% additional Aero damage for Jiyan's damage window.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Offers an unconditional 12% Aero DMG and Heavy ATK boost when used as the Main Echo, and additionally is a Summon-type echo making it easy to use in any character's rotation, which often makes it the best option for any character using the set.

Gives the same buffs as its Nightmare variant, but only after being transformed into, for a duration of 15 seconds. This Echo compensates by dealing close to double the damage of the Nightmare and giving more Energy to the character using it, but it's more difficult to incorporate into rotations, as it needs to be Swap Cancelled after the first hit to be used smoothly while making sure your character gets its buffs.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Jiyan's Signature is naturally his best weapon, as it grants him high Base ATK, alongside a lot of DMG Bonus to his main damage type being Heavy Attacks, and a CRIT DMG secondary stat to boot. A good blend of stats for a big damage increase compared to other weapons.

example_teams.team_notes: Only consider Ciaccona in the third slot with Jiyan on Windward Pilgrimage, Iuno in the team, and Ciaccona on her Signature Weapon.
Very strong in quickswap with Shorekeeper, can be equal to Jiyan's strongest team; Aero Rover is recommended for more casual players.

Only consider this team if Lynae and Mornye can't go anywhere else and Iuno isn't available - otherwise it may be a waste to spend such a strong universal buffing duo on Jiyan who has access to strong, free and permanent teammates.

cons: One of the oldest DPS characters in the game. Noticeably powercrept since release, struggles to clear endgame content when it becomes any difficult;
Signature weapon is basically necessary for him to clear any important endgame nowadays;
Can experience noticeable Energy issues depending on the enemy encounter and rotation used;
Almost incapable of hitting airborne enemies at all, strongly dislikes enemies with high mobility. Result: Jiyan straight-up doesn't function against a lot of boss enemies in the game.
pros: Strong AoE: Constant hits, and all Ultimate attacks group enemies;
One of the lowest Ultimate cooldowns in the game (16s) enable uniquely fast team rotations as his Ultimate allows him to access the majority of his damage;
Has good synergies with general buffers for Aero and Heavy Attack damage alike, as well as general Supports.

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Jiyan is a 5-star Aero main damage dealer and was the first Main DPS as well as first limited character to ever exist in the game. His kit is definitely reminiscent of the philosophy of the game's on-release days, not centred around any specific game mechanics other than dealing as much damage as possible within his Ultimate damage window, and general Heavy Attack-related buffs.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics & Rotation Concepts
paragraphs: Jiyan's rotation revolves around his Ultimate almost entirely. This is because his Ultimate makes him enter a special stance called Qingloong mode for 10s. In those 10s, he is able to cast special Qingloong Heavy Attacks, which deal way more damage than anything else in his kit. They represent the core of his damage and fitting in as many as he can in that 10s window is the goal of his rotation.

Jiyan's Forte is built up through his Intro or Basic Attacks. He holds up to 2 charges of "Resolve" (60 points, 30 per charge) that empower either his Skills or Ultimates when consumed. The increase on the empowered Skill is really minimal though, so what matters is the Ultimate. When cast, it deals no damage unless Jiyan holds a charge of Resolve, in which case he performs an opening attack that deals a good amount of damage. Jiyan also gains the enhancement on his Skill for free if he casts it during his Ultimate window.

Finally, Jiyan's passives are simple damage increases activated by Intro and hitting a target respectively, and his Outro enables him to cast 2 Coordinated Attacks for a bit more damage when other characters cast Heavy Attacks for 8s. Most of the time, this will only be triggered once per team rotation, though it's possible to go out of your way to trigger it a second time if you want.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: Jiyan has been an outdated DPS for a long time. It's fair to say that as a 1;x DPS, much like the other older members of the roster, he should not even be considered to pull if you care about the meta. His teams deal too little damage to be worth it, or require insane time/build investment to learn proper rotations with a good build. Generally, Jiyan is not recommended.

However, Jiyan does have two advantages if he's already on your account: He's Quickswap-friendly, and he doesn't need limited teammates to get close to his full potential. Sure, both Iuno and Ciaccona are upgrade paths, but Mortefi and Shorekeeper or Verina can suffice for clearing scores in low ToA floors or in Endstate Matrix. Don't count on him for Whimpering Wastes though; despite his AoE capabilities, he doesn't deal the damage required to keep up anymore.

There are two issues still: First, the elephant in the room, there are a lot of characters who can accomplish this other than Jiyan. Good examples of this are Jingran, Suoming, Augusta and so on. Even in the free character department, Encore and Havoc Rover can work decently with free teammates, to a degree that approaches Jiyan's. But they're permanently available and don't require a limited weapon to perform, unlike him.

Second, he pretty much cannot hit airborne enemies, and mobile enemies hurt his damage potential a lot as well. Even in his few use cases, he's limited in terms of what enemies he can actually attack properly, simply because his attacks don't connect against a lot of enemies in the game.

In conclusion, while Jiyan is not a recommended pull currently, if he's already on your account, you can still get some decent use out of him. In ToA or Endstate Matrix, he can still perform if you have him properly invested and some teammates available (which shouldn't be difficult as he has a good selection of free and limited teammates).

synergies.commentary: As a Heavy Attack Main DMG dealer, Jiyan can function with a variety of Heavy Attack DMG buffers to increase his damage, Iuno being the best overall as she provides the best mix of buffs and personal damage as well as an Aero element synergy. Phrolova is an excellent Dual DPS option who also mixes in some Heavy DMG buffing, while Rebecca and Mortefi are the more accessible Heavy DMG buffing options accessible for free.

These two are more unconventional buffer choices for Jiyan. Ciaccona can either work as an insanely strong secondary in Quickswap Jiyan compositions as none of her buffs expire upon swapping, which means Jiyan can switch in the middle of his Heavy Attacks for Ciaccona to do several complete attack combos while Jiyan is rotating. However, for more casual players, Ciaconna is also undeniably the best third slot teammate for Jiyan alongside Iuno, making for a strong Mono Aero team composition. Lynae is also a possible option alongside Mornye as the duo's generalist buffing potential is enough to outdo any F2P team choices, but will see rarer use as that duo is often better used elsewhere.

Jiyan works with all kinds of universal Support options. Shorekeeper and Verina are the most obvious picks as they offer a wide variety of generalist, non-specialized buffs that can increase the entire team's damage regardless of who they are. Mornye and Aero Rover are more niche, as Mornye will only see use alongside Rebecca and Lynae for Hack and Tune Rupture synergies respectively, while Aero Rover may be considered alongside Ciaccona outside of Quickswap compositions for an Aero Erosion synergy.
